title: Proverbs 12
paragraphs: ¹ Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is a fool. ² A good person earns the LORD's favor, but the LORD condemns those who scheme evil. ³ No one can be made secure by wickedness, but the roots of the righteous cannot be shaken. ⁴ A capable wife is a crown to her husband, but one who acts shamefully is like rot in his bones. ⁵ The plans of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.

⁶ The words of the wicked lie in ambush for blood, but the mouth of the upright rescues them. ⁷ The wicked are overthrown and are gone, but the house of the righteous stands firm. ⁸ A person is praised according to their wisdom, but those with a twisted heart are despised. ⁹ Better to be a nobody with a servant than to put on airs but have no food. ¹⁰ A righteous person cares for the life of their animal, but even the kindness of the wicked is cruel.

¹¹ Whoever works the land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies has no sense. ¹² The wicked desire the plunder of evildoers, but the root of the righteous produces fruit. ¹³ The wicked are trapped by their own words, but the righteous escape from trouble. ¹⁴ A person is satisfied with good things through the fruit of their mouth, and the work of their hands comes back to them. ¹⁵ The way of the fool is right in their own eyes, but whoever listens to advice is wise.

¹⁶ A fool's anger is known at once, but a prudent person overlooks an insult. ¹⁷ An honest witness tells the truth, but a false witness tells lies. ¹⁸ Reckless words pierce like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing. ¹⁹ Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment. ²⁰ Deceit fills the hearts of those who plot evil, but those who promote peace have joy.

²¹ No harm comes to the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble. ²² The LORD detests lying lips, but those who deal faithfully are his delight. ²³ A prudent person keeps their knowledge to themselves, but fools blurt out foolishness. ²⁴ Diligent hands will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor. ²⁵ Worry weighs down the heart, but a kind word lifts it up.

²⁶ The righteous person is a guide to their neighbor, but the path of the wicked leads them astray. ²⁷ A lazy man doesn't cook what he caught in the hunt, but the diligent person makes use of everything. ²⁸ In the path of righteousness is life, and on that road there is no death.
